text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The CEC savings bank accepts applications for loans at 15 percent subsidised interest starting Wednesday. The CEC will give loans worth 100 billion lei this year.
- Italian company SAIT Metalli won an auction for 25,000 tonnes of scrap iron sold off by Romania's national railway company SNCFR.
- The leu currency depreciated further over October 7-14 and is expected to breach the 3,300 to dollar threshold in the next few days.
- Romania resorted to international capital markets raisings to pay part of its foreign debt this year, and to strengthen forex reserves, central bank governor Mugur Isarescu says in interview.
ADEVARUL
- Foreign exchange rules and preferential credits are the two brakes to the growth of Romania's economy, the newspaper shows in a commentary.
- World Bank's International Finance Corporation will soon open office in Bucharest.
- Much of this year's sunflower and maize crops is still on fields as harvesting has been halted due to recent rainfalls.
AZI
- Trade Ministry increased sunflower oil export quotas this year to 165,000 tonnes from 75,000 tonnes.
LIBERTATEA
- Troubled private bank Banca Dacia Felix SA has two more weeks to wait before a court decides on its fate.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Romanian detergent maker Apollo SA started producing Henkel's Rex-brand detergents.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romanian oil exploration company Petrom RA and Enterprise Oil signed a contract to drill off Bulgaria, in the Black Sea.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Miners' trade unions leader says his labour union fears that ruling Party of Social Democracy may orchestrate massive vote rigging during November 3 polls.
- Opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) cannot enter coalitions before the November polls, said Radu Vasile, secretary general of National Peasant Party, CDR's backbone .
- Romania ranks first among European countries with highest infant mortality rate.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- United Nations' Development Programme (UNDP) to launch campaign to clean Bucharest with World Bank resident staffers, UNDP and other U.N. local staff expected to mop the streets.
ADEVARUL
- An army NCO beat up seven soldiers in barracks near Bucharest.
- Three main opposition groups -- CDR, Social Democrat Union and National Liberal Alliance -- failed to sign expected accord on cooperation to supervise elections.
- Some 1,000 members of the Romanian community in the U.S. staged rally in Chicago on Sunday to demand Romania's fast-track admission into NATO.
- State-owned Tarom airline refused to transport for free some 230,000 voting bulletins for Romanians living abroad.
- Romania became paradise for traders of counterfeit goods due to lack of quality control systems.
- Hungarian-born financier George Soros to visit Romania starting October 16.
LIBERTATEA
- Opposition is split ahead of November polls.
- Addicts smuggle drugs into hospitals, said Cristian Belu, head of drug addiction section of Gheorghe Marinescu hospital.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Public works ministry to build 17,500 social houses using foreign finance.
- CDR will form coalition cabinet after November 3 polls only with parties which agree with its government programme.
VOCEA ROMANIEI
- British Prime Minister John Major hails signature of Romanian-Hungarian treaty. ($=3,285 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
